title: The Wrong Bus
learning_objectives: Unseen transfer check: read a new text alone and answer without practice
Infer feelings and reasons from text evidence
parent_prompts: UNSEEN CHECK: do not preview this book with the child. Let them read it once, alone, then ask the questions. Record the result in parent.html > Evidence > Unseen-text check, not as a practice quiz.

pages.text: Ben got on the number four bus with his grandma. He liked the seat at the back, so he ran to it and sat down.
pages.illustration_brief: A boy running down the aisle of a bus toward the back seat; an older woman paying the driver.
pages.audio_script: Ben got on the number four bus with his grandma. He liked the seat at the back, so he ran to it and sat down.
pages.image_alt: A boy running down the aisle of a bus toward the back seat; an older woman paying the driver.

pages.text: The bus pulled away. Ben looked out of the window. The shops went past. The park went past. Then a street he did not know went past.
pages.illustration_brief: View through a bus window: shops, then a park, then an unfamiliar street with tall houses.
pages.audio_script: The bus pulled away. Ben looked out of the window. The shops went past. The park went past. Then a street he did not know went past.
pages.image_alt: View through a bus window: shops, then a park, then an unfamiliar street with tall houses.

pages.text: Ben turned round. The seat next to him was empty. Grandma was not on the bus.
pages.illustration_brief: Ben on the back seat, looking at the empty seat beside him, eyes wide.
pages.audio_script: Ben turned round. The seat next to him was empty. Grandma was not on the bus.
pages.image_alt: Ben on the back seat, looking at the empty seat beside him, eyes wide.

pages.text: His hands felt cold. He walked to the front, holding the poles. "Please," he said to the driver, "I think I lost my grandma."
pages.illustration_brief: Ben walking carefully down the aisle holding a pole, approaching the driver.
pages.audio_script: His hands felt cold. He walked to the front, holding the poles. Please, he said to the driver, I think I lost my grandma.
pages.image_alt: Ben walking carefully down the aisle holding a pole, approaching the driver.

pages.text: The driver smiled. "You did not lose her. You lost the bus. This is the number fourteen. Your grandma is on the number four, and I think she is looking for you right now."
pages.illustration_brief: The driver turning with a kind smile, pointing at a sign showing 14.
pages.audio_script: The driver smiled. You did not lose her. You lost the bus. This is the number fourteen. Your grandma is on the number four, and I think she is looking for you right now.
pages.image_alt: The driver turning with a kind smile, pointing at a sign showing 14.

pages.text: The driver stopped the bus and made a phone call. Ben sat on the front seat this time, right where the driver could see him.
pages.illustration_brief: The bus stopped at a kerb; the driver on a phone; Ben on the front seat.
pages.audio_script: The driver stopped the bus and made a phone call. Ben sat on the front seat this time, right where the driver could see him.
pages.image_alt: The bus stopped at a kerb; the driver on a phone; Ben on the front seat.

pages.text: Ten minutes later a number four bus pulled up behind them. Grandma got off, walking very fast. Ben had never been so glad to see anyone.
pages.illustration_brief: Grandma stepping quickly off a second bus; Ben running toward her.
pages.audio_script: Ten minutes later a number four bus pulled up behind them. Grandma got off, walking very fast. Ben had never been so glad to see anyone.
pages.image_alt: Grandma stepping quickly off a second bus; Ben running toward her.

pages.text: "Next time," said Grandma, hugging him, "we sit together. And we both read the number." "Four," said Ben. "Not fourteen."
pages.illustration_brief: Grandma hugging Ben beside the bus; a 4 and a 14 sign visible on the two buses.
pages.audio_script: Next time, said Grandma, hugging him, we sit together. And we both read the number. Four, said Ben. Not fourteen.
pages.image_alt: Grandma hugging Ben beside the bus; a 4 and a 14 sign visible on the two buses.

quiz.prompt: What was the number of the bus Ben got on by mistake?
quiz.explanation: Page 5: This is the number fourteen.

quiz.prompt: How did Ben feel when he saw the empty seat?
quiz.explanation: Grandma was not on the bus (page 3) and his hands felt cold (page 4). Cold hands are a sign of being scared.

quiz.prompt: Why was Grandma not on the bus?

options.text: Ben got on a different bus from her

quiz.explanation: Page 5: You lost the bus. Your grandma is on the number four.

quiz.prompt: Why did Ben sit at the front the second time?

options.text: So the driver could see him and he would be safe

quiz.explanation: Page 6: right where the driver could see him.

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up what went wrong and what Ben did that was sensible.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says he lost grandma; with support: wrong bus, with prompting; independent: got on 14 not 4, noticed she was missing, told the driver politely, sat where he could be seen
quiz.explanation: For an unseen check, note how much help was needed and whether the child cited the text.

off_screen_prompt: Next time you take a bus or a lift, read the number out loud before you get on.
